Public Transport and Road Investment

Many people debate about how governments should spend money on transport. Some people think that roads are more important, but other people think public transport is better. I believe that governments should prioritize spending on public transport to reduce congestion and help commuters, while still maintaining essential road networks to protect rural connections.

First, public transport is very important for cities. It is good because it gives affordability for commuters. Many people do not have money for cars, so they need cheap buses and trains. If governments spend money on this, it gives people access to jobs. Furthermore, public transport can move many people at the same time. This leads to lower congestion because fewer people will drive their own cars. But if the buses are slow, people will not use them, so governments must spend money to make them better.

On the other hand, roads are also necessary, especially for rural areas. People in the countryside do not have big bus networks or trains. Consequently, they must drive cars to go to work or go to the hospital. We must protect rural connections because these people need to travel too. If the government does not maintain the roads, the roads will become very bad and dangerous. This will make life very difficult for rural people who have no other choices.

In conclusion, I think governments should spend more money on public transport because it helps with congestion and helps poor commuters to get jobs. However, they should not stop spending on roads because roads are still needed to keep rural connections safe.

TASK RESPONSE · BAND 7.0

Task Response

The candidate appropriately addresses all parts of the prompt by discussing both public transport and road spending. A clear, consistent position is established in the introduction and maintained throughout the essay. Main ideas are extended and supported, but there is a slight tendency to over-generalise, such as asserting that rural residents have no other choices but to drive.

“I believe that governments should prioritize spending on public transport to reduce congestion and help commuters, while still maintaining essential road networks to protect rural connections.”
Your next step

Avoid absolute statements like 'no other choices' and instead use qualifying language to make the supporting arguments more precise and academically rigorous.

A revision of your writing
Your original
This will make life very difficult for rural people who have no other choices.
Suggested revision
This will make life exceptionally difficult for rural residents, who often lack viable alternative modes of travel.
The next band

To secure Band 8, the essay needs to avoid over-generalisations and provide more nuanced, well-supported arguments rather than simplified assertions about rural and urban commuters.
